sections.h2: Oil and product lines run near full, while gas estimates sit at 41 to 50%

chart.title: Product lines are well used, but both gas-network estimates are far lower
chart.sub: Utilisation of capacity, %. Different bases and dates; not directly comparable.
chart.source: Oil India FY2024-25 annual report; PNGRB monthly register; PNGRB chairman; IEEFA.
rows: Oil India Numaligarh–Siliguri product line, FY2024-25

sections.means: The 91.46% and 69.40% figures measure product lines, while the 50% and 41% gas figures come from different organisations and periods, so they are not like-for-like.
sections.todo: Plan expansion first where product lines already run past design capacity, which the post flags as a bottleneck risk.

sections.h2: Gas trunk pipelines are authorised for 34,200 km but operate about 25,400 km

chart.title: Gas trunk lines were authorised for about 8,800 km more than they operated
chart.source: Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas year-end reviews via PIB (June 2025).

sections.means: The gap reflects pipeline built ahead of confirmed gas supply and demand, a pattern the post traces to LNG and domestic supply that did not fully materialise.
sections.todo: Connect industrial clusters near trunk lines with spurs and city gas networks, the missing regional layer the post identifies.

sections.h2: The 75% use benchmark that unlocks PNGRB's reserve is above both gas estimates

chart.title: The reserve is funded only above 75% use, far above the gas averages
chart.source: PNGRB NGPL Tariff Regulations amendment (July 2025); PNGRB chairman; IEEFA.

sections.means: A reserve built to reward crossing 75% only makes sense if most gas lines are below it, which the post reads as the regulator admitting the shortfall.
sections.todo: Watch whether the three-year contract requirement and the reserve move gas utilisation toward 75% in the next PNGRB reports.
